title: Rethinking How We Move
sentences: Owning a car still feels, to many people, like an unavoidable part of adult life.
Yet in cities with reliable trains and buses, that assumption starts to fall apart.
Public transport can be slower, admittedly, but it removes the stress of driving entirely.
Whereas a car sits idle for most of the day, a bus carries dozens of passengers at once.
Nevertheless, many suburbs were built assuming that everyone would simply drive everywhere.
This design leaves people without cars feeling stranded and poorly served.
Cycling, meanwhile, has quietly become a serious alternative in several major cities.
It is cheap, it keeps you fit, and it rarely gets stuck in traffic during rush hour.
On the other hand, cyclists often feel unsafe where roads were never designed for them.
If governments invested more in safe cycling paths, far fewer people would need a car.
Rethinking how we move is not just personal choice but a matter of shared design.
